article.headline: Coyle wins first game as Liberty coach
article.story:
NEW YORK (AP) -- Pat Coyle was more concerned with the New York
Liberty improving their play than with winning in her debut as the
team's interim head coach.

Becky Hammon scored a season-high 26 points -- including four
over the final 31 seconds -- and the Liberty beat the Sacramento
Monarchs 73-66 Tuesday night in Coyle's first game since taking
over for the fired Richie Adubato.

"I want us playing well," Coyle said. "They were feeling the
effects of what happened this weekend, and they wanted so much to
do well for me. In one timeout I said 'I appreciate your effort but
we need to start playing relaxed and just play."

Vickie Johnson had 15 points and rookie Shameka Christon added a
season-high 12 points and six rebounds for New York, which closed
the game with 23-7 run over the final 7:43.

"I thought we looked more like ourselves toward the end of the
game," Coyle said. "We're still not anywhere near where we need
to be, but it was a better effort."

Yolanda Griffith had 17 points and Kara Lawson added 15 for
Sacramento, which has lost consecutive games after a three-game
winning streak.

Coyle, an assistant with the Liberty since 1998, was made
interim coach on Saturday after the team fired Adubato.

"It was important for us to get the win," Hammon said. "We
played with a lot of energy and we need to continue to play this
way."

New York, which lost 73-47 at Sacramento last Thursday in the
finale of a four-game road trip, won for just the second time in 10
games after a 6-1 start.

"They were on a long road trip, so maybe fatigue was a
factor," Griffith said. "We knew coming to New York it was going
to be a different story. There was a coaching change, so the
momentum was with them from the beginning."

Tied 30-all at halftime, the Monarchs went on an 11-2 run over
the opening 2:51 of the second half, capped by Lawson's fastbreak
layup.

New York closed it to 45-43 on Christon's layup with 12:51 left,
but Sacramento pushed its lead back to nine on Lawson's short
fadeaway for a 59-50 lead with 8 minutes remaining.

The Liberty then went on their game-ending run, started by a
3-pointer by Christon.

"They continually ran the high pick-and-roll with Becky and
various high post people to overcome our pressure," Monarchs coach
John Whisenant said. "We defended it on occasion for a while, but
late in the game Vickie Johnson and Becky got loose from us and got
some easy baskets when it really counted. You've got to give them a
lot of credit."
